key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent complex dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules from molecular structure, closely matching TD-DFT features at a fraction of the cost.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster screening of photoactive molecules and device-level optical simulation for organic optoelectronics without relying entirely on expensive quantum-chemical calculations.
method: Uses an equivariant GNN to learn tensor-valued, frequency-dependent polarizability from 3D geometry and UV-vis spectra.
Predicts both dispersive and absorptive components of the complex dynamic polarizability tensor.
Evaluated on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic molecules, then integrated into a downstream device simulation workflow.
evidence_signal: Across QM9 and Harvard OPV datasets, the model reproduced main spectral features and achieved strong agreement in device-level charge carrier generation rates with TD-DFT-based simulations ($R^2 = 0.94$).
watch_item: Performance may depend on the availability and quality of molecular geometries, spectra, and representative training data for out-of-distribution chemistry.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
